findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, and the new crates/athena-cli/tests/status_durations.rs.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list names status.rs but not display.rs. display.rs was a planned file, and the 3-line edit is what makes `athena status` print the line, which criterion 5 needs. The planned display test was put in a new integration test file instead of display.rs. Both are needed to show part 3 and add no other behaviour.

findings.summary: Runs that time out never appear in the status durations report.
findings.evidence: The early return for a held job writes no Verification record, and check_durations reads only verification.checks. So the report can never include the runs that hit the limit; it shows the climb towards the limit, not the kills. The reading accepted this (finding (c)), and the duration is still in the closing reason.

summary: The change does all three parts the retry asked for. First, athena.toml sets check_timeout_s = 1800, and config.rs is untouched. Second, a check killed at its deadline, when it is the only new failure, now ends the job as a resumable environment stop. The reason reads 'environment: check timed out: test ran Ns of Ms limit', and the job stops before the verifier runs. A real nonzero failure, or a timeout beside a real failure, is still rejected, and failures that were already present on the base commit are handled as the verdict handles them. Third, `athena status` prints the median and slowest test-check durations over the newest 20 jobs against the limit, with an 'over 80%' flag. I ran the 10 new athena-core tests and the new CLI status test, and all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs pass too. The hold copies the existing low-disk early return and sorts runs by their own exit code and deadline note, not by a guess, so I found no soundness problem. There are two minor findings. display.rs and a new CLI test file are outside the deliverables list, though both are needed for the status line. And jobs held for a timeout write no check record, so the status report never shows the runs that hit the limit; the reading accepted this.
